sources.entry: debugpy - A Debug Adapter Protocol debugger for Python, used by VS Code for remote debugging.

summary.one_liner: debugpy is Microsoft's Debug Adapter Protocol implementation for Python 3, used to debug scripts and modules remotely or attach to running processes.
use_cases: Debugging a Python script from VS Code or another DAP client
Remote debugging a Python program over a network port
Attaching a debugger to an already running Python process by PID
Pausing a program at breakpoint() or on a caught exception
notable: Runs as a DAP server so any DAP-compatible client can connect, with VS Code as the named example
Command-line mode can launch a script or module with debugging enabled, or inject into a running process by PID
Python API offers listen(), wait_for_client(), breakpoint(), and trigger_exception_handler() for in-code control
Thread behavior is configurable per launch via stopAllThreadsOnSuspend and steppingResumesAllThreads
Logs go to debugpy*.log files via --log-to or DEBUGPY_LOG_DIR
caveats: Listening on 0.0.0.0 lets anyone who can reach the port execute arbitrary code in the debugged process; the README says use only on secure networks
Thread-suspension settings apply only to client launch/attach requests, not to the CLI switches or debugpy.configure()
Coverage table lists Windows, Linux and Mac but the cells are empty, so platform support is not stated in the README
